newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM SAYS KONKOLA STUDY TO BE DONE BY SEPT.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM SAYS KONKOLA STUDY TO BE DONE BY SEPT.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) said on Friday it expected an international consortium to complete due diligence and feasibility studies into Zambia's Konkola Deep copper project next month.
The consortium, led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa, started an investigation into the project after signing a memorandum of understanding with the Zambian government in February this year.
Other members of the consortium were Gencor Ltd and Falconbridge Ltd , but Gencor withdrew in May.
"It is hoped that by the end of September this year, the consortium would conclude its feasibility study," ZCCM chairman Luke Mwananshiku said in a statement.
The consortium said early this year it would cost between $700 million and $800 million to develop the mine.

The development of Konkola Deep is seen as crucial to the future of Zambia's mining industry, as the Nchanga open pit mine - the mainstay of the industry at present - is expected to run out of ore at the end of the century.
Mwananshiku said he expected the government to conclude negotiations on the sale of ZCCM assets by December 31 this year.
"It is expected that the rest of the negotiations will be concluded between July 1 and December 31, 1997," Mwananshiku said.
"It is hoped that lenders to the company would consent to its privatisation and allow the new owners to assume the debt," he added.
The mining conglomerate owes creditors some $600 million. The privatisation of ZCCM assets got underway in January when Cyprus Amax Minerals company of the United States acquired Kansanshi mine.
In June, the government awarded the Binani Group the Luanshya/Baluba mining and metallurgical complex.
The Metorex consortium was awarded the Chibuluma mine assets in July.
